Our story

More than a home.
A place to belong.

A child needs more than a roof. Every child deserves to be safe, encouraged, educated and treated with dignity.

Charity Ewela Nakowa Orphanage Home is based at No. 70 UTAN GRA, Jos, Plateau State. The home supports children with daily care and opportunities to learn, develop and build confidence.

Our work is grounded in a simple belief: when a community makes room for its children, hope has somewhere to grow.

Meet the woman behind the mission
THE HEART OF THE HOMEHajiya Bilkisu Musa

Biography · Leadership

One caring heart
can change many lives.

Hajiya Bilkisu Musa began her sports career as a wrestler in Bauchi State in 1988. From wrestling, she transitioned to Judo and Boxing, earning employment as a brown-belt Judoka and Silver Medalist in Boxing in 1989 with the Bauchi State Sports Council.

Read more↓

In 1990, she moved to Jos, Plateau State, where she gained employment with the Plateau State Sports Council as a weightlifter. Competing for Plateau State, she won 42 Gold Medals and became unbeatable within the Nigerian Weightlifting Federation — never Silver nor Bronze, Gold was always her target.

In 1995, she made history as the first woman in Africa to win Silver at the World Senior Weightlifting Championship held in Guangzhou, China from November 16–26, 1995. This achievement marked the beginning of her international journey in weightlifting.

In 1997, at the World Weightlifting Championship in Chiang Mai, Thailand (December 6–14, 1997), she won Silver for Nigeria. In 1999, at the World Weightlifting Championship at the Peace and Friendship Stadium in Piraeus, Athens, Greece (November 21–28, 1999), she lifted a total of 252.5kg to finish as the world's third best.

During the 7th All African Games in Johannesburg, South Africa in 1999, she won three Gold Medals for Nigeria and set three African Records in Snatch, Jerk and Total. In the same competition, the Nigerian Female Weightlifting Team won 21 Gold Medals.

In 2003, during the All African Games in Abuja tagged COJA 2003, she placed fourth due to technical issues. The same year, at the 1st Afro-Asian Games in India, she won three Silver Medals for Nigeria and set a Commonwealth Games Record. In 2003, at the Olympic Qualifier in Canada, her points contribution enabled the Nigerian team to secure two Olympic seats. From there, she decided to retire to pave the way for upcoming weightlifters like Maryam Usman to continue in her category.

After retirement, she did not stop. She has produced a generation of African and Commonwealth record holders including Chineye Fidelis, Ijeoma Nwanyi, Hadiza Zakari and Fatima Otiameh Musa.

Currently, Chief Hajiya Bilkisu Musa is a promoter in the sport of weightlifting and Founder of the Charity Ewela Nakowa Sports Development Club — now hosting its third edition of Weightlifting Championships — and Founder of the Charity Ewela Nakowa Orphanage Home at No 70 UTAN GRA, Jos.

“We do not have much, but we have enough to share — and sharing makes it warm.”— A message of care from the home
